chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Joining Lionel Hampton and the pay dispute
summary: Hampton agreed to $400 a week; Gladys Hampton cut it to $125 on the road in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: We haven't talked too much about me coming up in jazz and the things I had to go through.
I had to go through one of the lowest band leaders in the world, Lionel Hampton, where everybody in

America loved him, because he was a showman, jump and down, on his drums. He didn't care about his playing too much. He came in and asked me to join the band. Joe Comfort left to go to Lionel Hampton -- Joe Comfort left to go with Nat King Cole. And he asked me to That's when he joined the band.

And I said, "How much money you pay you?" He said, "How much what you want?" I said, I want $400 a week." And he says, "That's fine, I'll pay you that." This is in California where he was playing a theater there. So I joined the band. I worked locally, like San Francisco and places like that, he paid me this money. Okay, Here we go to Chicago, I get called to the office and Gladys Hampton said, "There's some mistake in your payroll." Lionel ?s She said, That's his wife, Gladys Hampton is his wife. Say, "How much has Lionel been paying you? I said, $400 a week, for everything, one-nighters, everything. $400 every week."

She said, "We don't pay anybody that kind of money, Milt Buckner, Bobby Plater Britt not even (unintelligible) the first alto player, Woodman, none of the guys get that kind of money.. Said, "there's some mistake, Lionel must have misunderstood you." Said, "We've got to take all that money back, he overpaid you." I'm in Chicago, you know?

So it's not too easy to quit. So she she said, "The most I can pay you is $125 a week. I said, $125 on the road? You must be crazy." So I started really putting a show on the band, get drunk, fight with everybody. Those two people are the most
